candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, participate in quality-improvement systems, and use organizational resources to promote safe client care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — role of infection-prevention program leadership
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize infection-prevention program leadership as an ongoing systems role that integrates surveillance, policy implementation, performance monitoring and feedback, and healthcare-personnel education rather than functioning only during outbreaks.

options.A: Coordinate HAI and pathogen surveillance, monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, support current evidence-based policies, and provide or coordinate staff education and feedback.
options.B: Provide routine bedside assignments as the primary function and become involved in infection prevention only during declared outbreaks.
options.C: Track infection rates but avoid participating in policy, staff education, or performance-improvement activities because those functions belong exclusively to unit managers.
options.D: Focus only on employee illness records and exclude patient-care infection risks and healthcare-associated infections from the program.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices call for qualified personnel to manage facility infection-prevention programs. Core program activities include monitoring healthcare-associated infections and transmission, monitoring adherence to infection-prevention requirements, providing feedback, ensuring current evidence-based policies and procedures, and providing job-specific education and training. B incorrectly limits the role to outbreak response. C fragments functions that CDC treats as components of the infection-prevention program. D confuses a facility-wide infection-prevention program with occupational health alone.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A facility infection-prevention program is managed by qualified IPC personnel and includes ongoing surveillance, evidence-based policy support, staff education, monitoring of practice adherence, feedback, and response to identified transmission risks.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; Isolation Precautions — Fundamental Elements Needed to Prevent Transmission
candidate.source_locator: Core Practices Table — Leadership Support: assign qualified individuals trained in infection prevention and control to manage the facility IPC program. Education and Training: provide job-specific IPC education and current evidence-based written policies/procedures. Performance Monitoring and Feedback: monitor adherence to IPC practices and infection incidence, provide regular feedback, and use surveillance to detect transmission. Isolation Precautions, Surveillance for HAIs: surveillance is an essential ongoing systematic activity for identifying infections, clusters, and indications for change.
